newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end strong after see-saw session.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end strong after see-saw session.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended stronger on Thursday after see-sawing in a wide range, caught between optimism after Wednesday's surge in prices and caution ahead of the release of fresh U.S. economic data, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index rose 72.09 points to 12,477.56 after slipping into negative territory early in the session to a low of 12,377.88 and rising to an afternoon high of 12,496.57.

"On the one hand local shares just followed yesterday's rebound and continue to fare quite well, but on the other hand I think investors are still concerned about the U.S. figures," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng index rose 213.30 points on Wednesday.
Market turnover was HK$6.34 billion on Thursday, down from Wednesday's HK$7.48 billion.
September U.S. personal income and consumption data are due on Thursday and the October U.S. jobs report on Friday.

"I think the market has made its move for this week and I think it is going to sit around and wait for some of the data coming out," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
